t: Section 105(f)(1)(B)(ix) of the Compact of Free Association Amendments Act of 2003 (48 U.S.C. 1921d(f)(1)(B)(ix)) shall be applied by substituting “2017” for “2016”.

fable.w: The section only extends a date in a cross-referenced provision of the Compact of Free Association Amendments Act by substituting "2017" for "2016". It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. The only tempting reading is that the Compact involves foreign governments, but nothing in this text calls for consulting or coordinating with any non-federal party before a federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statute, changing a specific year from 2016 to 2017. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely a legislative update to existing law.
qwen_block.s: Section 105(f)(1)(B)(ix) of the Compact of Free Association Amendments Act of 2003 (48 U.S.C. 1921d(f)(1)(B)(ix)) shall be applied by substituting “2017” for “2016”.

opus.w: This section only changes a date in an existing law, substituting "2017" for "2016" in 48 U.S.C. 1921d(f)(1)(B)(ix). It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The mention of the Compact of Free Association is a citation, not a process that brings outsiders into a decision.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section cites the Compact of Free Association Amendments Act, and a compact is an arrangement with foreign governments. That might suggest outside parties are involved. But the text only changes a date in an existing provision. No consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue is created, so no outside party takes part in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment that changes a specific year in a previous statute. It does not create any mechanism for consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties. It does not establish an advisory committee, require public comment, or grant rights to sue. It is purely a legislative adjustment of a deadline.
qwen_chat.s: Section 105(f)(1)(B)(ix) of the Compact of Free Association Amendments Act of 2003 (48 U.S.C. 1921d(f)(1)(B)(ix)) shall be applied by substituting “2017” for “2016”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing a date in a statute involving a Compact of Free Association (which involves non-federal entities like the Freely Associated States) implies some form of consultation or participation. However, the text itself is merely a technical amendment to a deadline. It does not establish a process for consultation, create an advisory body, require public comment, or grant rights to outside parties. It is a legislative housekeeping provision.
